prompt:
Re-design epic manager-agent-flow-event-driven (supersede the 2026-08-25 design with a re-verified one). Read the full brief first: /Users/gavingolden/code/me/flow/.flow-tmp/manager-epic-redesign-brief.md

CLARIFICATION ROUND ANSWERS (owner, 2026-10-25 — binding):
1. Scope: EPIC-FIRST, FLEET LATER. MVP is a singleton manager per epic: launches frontiers with coordination context, detects sibling conflicts, surfaces gated PRs. The old fleet-wide autonomy goal (self-resolving plan-review/clarification pauses across all pipelines/repos) becomes a later/optional feature or is cut — decide per the re-review evidence.
2. Autonomy (owner's verbatim answer): "i want it to have high autonomy and answer/drive high confidence questions for me. Subjective checks like the UI. User-facing behavior can be driven by the agent as long as it has high confidence. If not then the feature pipeline itself should be the place where I answer those questions and the orchestrator monitors it until I drive the feature pipeline. does that make sense?"
   → Interpretation to design against: the manager answers/drives pipeline questions (plan approval, clarifications, interview answers, and even SUBJECTIVE/UI sign-offs on user-facing behavior) when it has HIGH confidence. When not high-confidence, it does NOT relay the question to itself or a side channel — it leaves the question in the feature pipeline's own window for the owner to answer there, and the manager monitors that pipeline until the owner drives it, then resumes orchestrating. NOTE the tension with the brief's hard rule 5 ("never tick a SUBJECTIVE/owner sign-off unless the owner explicitly says so for that PR"): the owner is now granting a standing, confidence-gated delegation. The design must make that delegation explicit and opt-in (per epic / per manager start), define how "high confidence" is decided and calibrated (and what evidence a SUBJECTIVE/UI sign-off requires — e.g. screenshots/UI critique evidence, not vibes), leave an auditable trail of every question the manager answered on the owner's behalf, and keep the remaining hard rules intact (never override a gated verdict produced by validation itself without the delegation rules; never modify shared resources — shared DB rows, usage counters — or prod without owner approval; honor per-model/effort choices). Surface any residual tension in Open Questions rather than silently weakening a rule.
3. Non-epic siblings: IN SCOPE. The manager watches every live pipeline in the epic's repo for cross-pipeline conflicts (file ownership, shared local DB/resets/re-seeds, per-user spend/generation caps, serialized eval spend, judge-hash/calibration-marker invalidation), not only the epic's own features, and tells each pipeline about its siblings.

Additional requirements from the brief (must appear in design.md):
- A short "Re-review of the 2026-08-25 design" section: per old feature (f1–f6), keep / change / cut / already-shipped, each with evidence (file paths, PR numbers, harness primitives) verified against current flow main and the current Claude Code harness.
- Consider at least one radically simpler alternative (e.g. manager = a Workflow script, or a /loop'd plain session + helpers) next to the full event-driven agent; rank options by value, token cost and wall-clock; say why you chose.
- Check overlap/ordering with epic modernize-flow-s-supervisor-architecture (6/8 merged; f7-workflow-observability-floor ready, f8 blocked) and avoid collisions with the running pipeline add-ui-ux-critique-improve.
- Supersede the old epic explicitly (mechanics your call — e.g. mark the old manifest superseded/delete it in this same design PR); do not leave two live epics for one goal. If you edit/delete the old epic's files under .flow/epics/manager-agent-flow-event-driven/, do it in the worktree below and say so in your summary.
- Field-evidence items 1–7 in the brief (singleton discovery, coordination file, `flow epic launch` seed text, merge-guard override friction, hard rules, durable on-disk state across compaction/restart, terse impact-first status + model/effort honoring) are requirements to verify and address or explicitly cut with rationale.
- The owner asked that this re-design be reviewed at Opus 5.5 / high effort, and for that epic's features a per-model/effort choice of opus/high — record model/effort hints in manifest flowNewHints if the schema supports it.

features.title: `flow epic manage <slug>`: a zero-token sequencer that launches, holds back, and reports
features.description:
Add `flow epic manage <slug>`: a deterministic Bun sequencer for one approved epic that launches ready features, holds back unsafe launches, and shows a terse board, spending zero model tokens. It runs in the foreground of its own tmux window `manage-<slug>` (tmux-only, like every epic surface; refuse under plain shell with the existing named notice) and never touches the epic-design session's `<slug>` window or `~/.flow/state/<slug>.json`. Loop: poll every `~/.flow/state/*.json` belonging to the epic's repo every 2-5 s (epic features and non-epic siblings) and GitHub every 60-120 s with ONE batched query per repo per poll (merged / CI-concluded state for every watched PR and every open PR, so out-of-band merges are seen); on any change run the existing pure `reconcile()` + `classifyEvent()` (`bin/lib/epic-reconcile.ts`, which already floors on the committed status board), compute the frontier (`computeFrontier` in `bin/flow-epic-dag.ts`), and launch up to `epic.maxParallel` through `launchFeature()` / `flow epic launch` (`bin/lib/epic-launch.ts`). Drift guard (the reason PR #420 deleted the 2026-07 watch loop: it trusted `run.json`): before each launch run a mechanical duplicate check — no PR, branch, worktree, or live state file for the feature's id-derived slug or its `--epic <slug>/<id>` tag — and on any ambiguity (an `orphan` row, an unbound PR or branch, a manifest/run.json mismatch) do NOT launch or repair that node; show `drift: run /flow-epic-run reconcile-drift` on the board and keep launching independent branches. Never add judgment, retries, redirects, budgets, or a phase machine. State in `~/.flow/state/managers/<slug>/` (outside `listStates()`): `manager.json` {pid, procStartedAt, heartbeatAt, autonomy, startedAt} written under `withFileLockSync` (`bin/lib/lock.ts`), and one append-only `log.jsonl` (launch, hold, drift-halt, merged-observed, plus later delegated-decision entries). Singleton by state liveness (`bin/lib/liveness.ts`): a second `flow epic manage <slug>` while one is live refuses and prints the window name and how to switch to it. `flow epic status <slug>` and `flow ls` show the live sequencer and its heartbeat age (stale beyond 3 poll intervals). Board: the pause-output contract's impact-first slots, one line per feature that needs the owner (`gated`, `needs-human`, a pending pause) naming the window where they answer, plus one `flow-notify` per new owner-needed event; the epic ends with a final board when `reconcile()` says done. Ctrl-C (async sleep — the #390 loop swallowed SIGINT) and window close stop it with no effect on launched pipelines; a restart rebuilds from disk and GitHub. Manifest: make `flowNewHints.model` a typed `ModelAlias` hint in `bin/lib/epic-manifest-schema.ts`, mapped in `buildFeatureCreateArgs` (CLI `--model` > hint > config); add an optional typed `waitFor` string on Feature — a node with `waitFor` is never launched (`flow epic launch` refuses it with a named error, so `/flow-epic-run` cannot launch it either), shows on the board as `waiting on: <waitFor>`, and completes only via `flow epic bind <epic> <id> --external "<ref>"`. Model/effort flags, mirroring `flow feature create` / `flow epic create` / `flow epic run`: `flow epic manage <slug> [--model <opus|haiku|sonnet|fable>] [--effort <low|medium|high|xhigh|max>]`, validated by the same alias/level parsers those commands use, persisted in `manager.json` {model, effort} (precedence: flag > `config.models.manager` / `config.efforts.manager` > opus/high), shown on the board header, and listed in help and completions. They set (a) the model/effort of every model call made on the manager's behalf — the delegated-judgment `flow-claude-headless` calls later features add read them from `manager.json` — and (b) the fallback for a launched feature that has no manifest `model`/`effort` hint (per-feature precedence: `flow epic launch` CLI override > manifest hint > manager flag > config). The sequencer loop itself still makes zero model calls. `--autonomy observe` is the only autonomy value this feature accepts (the flag exists so a later feature can add `high`). Governance in lockstep: AGENTS.md and `.claude/rules/flow-supervisor-contracts.md` name `flow epic manage` as a sanctioned zero-fan-out, zero-form, never-merges surface; `docs/target-architecture.md`'s 'not a long-running daemon' line names this one owner-started foreground exception; `skills/pipeline/flow-epic-run/SKILL.md` gets one hands-table row pointing at the sequencer (its no-loop invariants stay true of the playbook itself); help, completions; rewrite the stale 'watch loop' comments in `bin/lib/epic-launch.ts`. Tests next door: reconcile-driven launch matrix over fixture state dirs, the three PR #420 drift scenarios (recreated slug, out-of-band merge, manifest drift) plus an unknown-slug pipeline for an epic feature (all must halt, not launch), `waitFor` refusal, singleton refusal, SIGINT exit, heartbeat staleness, gh-failure degradation to a board line, and a repo-scoping test (another repo's state never counts).

Part of epic `re-design-epic-manager-agent` (feature `f1-epic-sequencer`) — design at `.flow/epics/re-design-epic-manager-agent/design.md`.
features.rationale: Hides D1-D3: the deterministic poll/reconcile/launch loop, the drift and duplicate checks that answer why PR #420 deleted the 2026-07 loop, the manager state file and log, the typed model hint, and waitFor nodes.
acceptanceCriteria: WHEN the frontier is non-empty and in-flight features are below epic.maxParallel THE SYSTEM SHALL launch the next feature through flow epic launch with the manifest model and effort hints (fixture test asserts the argv)

WHEN a pipeline's state file changes phase THE SYSTEM SHALL redraw the board within 10 seconds, and WHEN a watched PR merges it SHALL observe it within 120 seconds using one batched GitHub query per repo per poll

WHEN any of the three PR #420 drift scenarios (recreated slug, out-of-band merge, manifest drift) or an unknown-slug pipeline for an epic feature is present THE SYSTEM SHALL not launch that feature and SHALL show a reconcile-drift line naming /flow-epic-run
WHEN a feature has a waitFor value THE SYSTEM SHALL never launch it, and flow epic launch SHALL refuse it with a named error
WHEN flow epic manage runs while the epic's manager.json shows a live sequencer THE SYSTEM SHALL refuse and print the live window name, and flow epic status and flow ls SHALL show its heartbeat age
WHEN the sequencer receives SIGINT THE SYSTEM SHALL exit 0 within one second without touching any launched pipeline, and a restart SHALL rebuild the same board from disk
WHEN the sequencer runs idle for an hour THE SYSTEM SHALL make zero model calls (no claude or flow-claude-headless spawn in the test seam)

WHEN flow epic manage runs with --model and --effort THE SYSTEM SHALL validate them like flow epic create, persist them in manager.json, show them on the board, and pass them to a launched feature only when that feature's manifest has no model/effort hint (fixture test asserts both argv cases)

features.title: The executive: an owner charter, an executive review that approves, presses, or defers, and the owner grant that lets it act
features.rationale: Hides D8: how the owner's perspective is written down, how an executive review decides act / challenge / defer, and the grant that lets that decision stand in for the owner's keystroke. Root because it needs no sequencer: /flow-epic-run uses it the day it merges.
acceptanceCriteria: WHEN an owner grant is live for an epic and one of its features reaches plan approval THE SYSTEM SHALL run the executive review before pausing and, on an approve decision whose hard preconditions pass, continue without pausing, record the decision with rationale, confidence and door type, print the disclosure line, and stamp the PR body

WHEN the executive review returns challenge THE SYSTEM SHALL run the pipeline's own plan revision pass with the challenge memo as the redirect and re-review, repeating while each round closes at least one blocking challenge, and SHALL decide approve or defer once a round closes none

WHEN the executive review returns defer, or any hard precondition fails, or the decision is a one-way door THE SYSTEM SHALL pause in the pipeline's own window as today with the executive's single recommendation and the one-word replies that accept or reject it
WHEN no grant is live, or the slug is not a feature of the granted epic THE SYSTEM SHALL never run a delegated decision
WHEN the owner corrects a delegated decision THE SYSTEM SHALL let that correction be added as a line in the charter section of the user-level product brief, which every later executive review reads

WHEN /flow-epic-run takes a step and a feature merged since the last step THE SYSTEM SHALL run one executive wave review, apply a reorder of unstarted features, and show any defer / cut / add / goal change only as a proposal for the owner

WHEN the executive review runs THE SYSTEM SHALL use the model and effort resolved like the manager's model: the sequencer's `--model`/`--effort` when it passes them, else `config.models.manager` / `config.efforts.manager`, else opus/high, stay within a per-call budget cap, and pause rather than decide when the call fails or is skipped
WHEN the executive's confidence is medium or low, or the door is one-way THE SYSTEM SHALL pause in the pipeline's own window exactly as today
features.description:
Give the manager a brain: the owner's perspective written down once, an executive review that applies it at decision points, and an owner grant that lets the review's decision stand in for the owner's keystroke. Owner charter: extend the user-level product brief (`~/.flow/product.md`, seeded by `bin/lib/product-brief-seed.ts`, read by `flow-product-brief`) with a `## Deciding on my behalf` section holding the charter in the epic design's `## Executive charter` (goal-first, question the premise, ruthless prioritization, simplicity unless later change is expensive, two-way vs one-way doors, press don't rubber-stamp, outside view + pre-mortem, accountability, owner rulings win, bias to action); update the seed so new installs get it; never fork a second values file. Executive review: new bare-name helper `flow-exec-review` (`bin/flow-exec-review.ts`, registered in `bin/lib/modules.ts`, pre-approved in `bin/lib/pipeline-allow-rules.ts`) with `review --kind plan|wave --epic <slug> [--slug <feature>]`: assembles a bounded decision packet the feature agent does not have — the epic goal and design, the manifest neighbourhood, the product brief + charter, the charter's standing corrections and prior decisions from the epic log, sibling pipeline phases, the plan or merged PR, and the cross-model review — and makes ONE `flow-claude-headless` call (model/effort resolved like the manager's model: the sequencer's `--model`/`--effort` when it passes them, else `config.models.manager` / `config.efforts.manager`, else opus/high; `--max-budget-usd` capped, read-only tools) returning a schema-validated envelope {decision: approve|challenge|defer (plan) or continue|reorder|propose|escalate (wave), doorType: two-way|one-way, confidence, rationale, challenges[] (blocking; no count cap; each names the decision it changes, the evidence that would settle it, and the cost of being wrong), notes[] (non-blocking; never trigger a revision round), recommendation}. Hard preconditions it never waives (mechanical, checked before the call): the cross-model plan review ran with a non-Claude reviewer engaged; every `[anchor: …]` resolves; `flow-plan-lint` clean; no proposed production, shared-database, usage-counter, or shared-service action (always one-way, always defer). Grant: `flow epic grant <epic> --autonomy high|off` (owner-typed CLI; `off` withdraws it) writes `~/.flow/state/managers/<epic>/grant.json` {epic, classes:[plan], grantedAt, grantedBy: owner-cli} (no model/effort: one model source, the owner's manager setting) under `withFileLockSync`; f1's sequencer later reads the same directory. Pipeline: in `skills/pipeline/flow-pipeline/references/phases/step-04-approval.md` (and its SKILL.md pointer), BEFORE rendering `plan-pending-review`, an epic feature with a live grant runs `flow-exec-review review --kind plan`; approve ⇒ append the decision to `~/.flow/state/managers/<epic>/log.jsonl`, print `Approved by the epic executive under your grant (decision <id>)`, stamp the PR body draft, continue past `checkpoint-pending-clear`; challenge ⇒ the existing revision pass with the challenge memo as the redirect, re-review, repeating while each round closes at least one blocking challenge; a round that closes none stops and decides or defers with the open points (runaway backstop: 4 rounds, logged); every challenge is logged with whether it was acted on, so the acted-on rate can tighten the bar; defer/fail ⇒ the normal pause with the recommendation and one-word replies. Interviews and clarifications are not delegated. Confidence uses flow's existing `[confidence: high|medium|low]` vocabulary: the executive acts only on high confidence AND a two-way door; anything else pauses in the feature window as today. Decision record: no new store — the f1 `log.jsonl` line, the PR-body stamp, and the board digest; an owner correction becomes a line the owner (or the session, on the owner's say-so) adds to the charter section, which every review reads. The charter is always read from the user-level `~/.flow/product.md`, even in a repo whose own `.flow/product.md` shadows the user brief for product review (`bin/flow-product-brief.ts` resolves repo-first). `/flow-epic-run`: add a wave-review step to launch-next (one `flow-exec-review review --kind wave` per newly observed merge; the decision is continue / reorder / propose / escalate: a reorder of unstarted features is a two-way door the playbook applies and logs; deferring or cutting a feature, adding one, or changing the epic goal is never applied — it is a proposal shown to the owner with its rationale, and an owner `yes` routes it through amend-manifest) — the executive reorders on its own and proposes every reshape. Write the review prompt in `references/executive-review.md` (charter text not duplicated — it is read from the product brief) and lint its hard-rule anchors in `bin/skill-md-lint.test.ts` (never merge, never `--record-override`, never answer prod/shared-resource actions, never send-keys, owner rulings win). Tests next door: envelope schema, every hard precondition's fail path, one-way door ⇒ defer, no-progress stop and the 4-round backstop, notes never trigger a round, acted-on logging, grant scope (non-epic or other-epic slug never passes), budget/headless failure ⇒ pause, charter read from the user-level brief even when a repo brief exists, propose never mutates the manifest, and the record/stamp shape. Shared with f1: the `~/.flow/state/managers/<epic>/` directory and `log.jsonl` line format — whichever merges second adopts the first's shape.

Part of epic `re-design-epic-manager-agent` (feature `f5-executive-judgment`) — design at `.flow/epics/re-design-epic-manager-agent/design.md`.

features.title: One manager home: scope, scoped grants, expiring notes, a scope-free decision log, and launch rulings
features.description:
Give the single global manager a deterministic home that is not tied to an epic, and replace the per-epic coordination file. No model calls; everything here is plain Bun and files. (1) Home: `~/.flow/manager/` holding `scope.json` (which pipelines, epics, and repos the manager may act on — written by `flow manage --scope …` and by the owner's words in the manager window, read before every message the manager sends), `grants.json`, `notes.jsonl`, `log.jsonl`, `proposals.json`, and a regenerated `status.md`. It lives outside `~/.flow/state/` so `listStates()` never lists it. (2) Scoped grants: generalize f5's `flow epic grant <epic> --autonomy high|off` into `flow grant <scope> --autonomy high|off [--delegate-ui] [--expires <dur>]`, where `<scope>` is `pipeline:<slug>`, `epic:<slug>`, or `repo:<name>` (no `all`); TTY-only exactly like f5's grant, with the same deny rules so no agent can write the file; `flow grant --list` prints live grants. f5's in-pipeline check resolves the most specific live grant covering the pipeline (pipeline > epic > repo). `flow epic grant` stays as a thin alias for `flow grant epic:<slug>`. (3) Decision log: move the shared `bin/lib/epic-manager-log.ts` (written by f1 and f5 under `~/.flow/state/managers/<epic>/log.jsonl`) to `~/.flow/manager/log.jsonl`; every entry carries `slug`, optional `epic`, and `repo`; per-epic readers filter by `epic` (no compatibility shim — flow has no users). (4) Notes: `flow-manager-note add --about <slug>[,<slug>] --text …` appends a transient coordination note ("W is seeding the local DB; Z waits"); a note expires when every pipeline it names is terminal. No committed `.flow/coordination-notes.json`: lasting repo rules belong in that repo's AGENTS.md. (5) Pruning is a rule, never model discretion: `flow-manager-prune` (run on every manager pass and by `flow manage` at start) drops expired notes, rolls log entries older than 90 days into per-month counts by kind and outcome (the acted-on calibration counts survive), and never touches an open proposal. (6) Proposals: `proposals.json` holds every open proposal (epic changes, stale-pipeline cancels, drafted interview answers) until the owner answers it; `status.md` is regenerated from state files on every pass (pipeline, repo, epic, phase, owner action, waiting age). (7) Launch rulings: `flow epic launch <epic> <id> --context-file <path>` appends a delimited 'Rulings and context' block before the pointer sentence of the seed; the block states that rulings marked DECIDED are binding on product calls and open to evidence-based technical correction, with every deviation reported in the PR's `## Deviations from plan`. Tests next door: grant scope resolution and precedence, TTY refusal, log move and epic filtering, note expiry, prune roll-up keeps counts, open proposals never pruned, `--context-file` placement before the pointer sentence.

Part of epic `re-design-epic-manager-agent` (feature `f2-manager-home`) — design at `.flow/epics/re-design-epic-manager-agent/design.md`.
features.rationale: Hides where the manager's memory lives and how it is pruned, and how authority is scoped (pipeline / epic / repo) — the deterministic half of the global manager, so f3's model session never owns state that only lives in a conversation. Replaces the cut per-repo coordination file (owner 2026-11-03: committed notes grow without bound and go stale).
acceptanceCriteria: WHEN the owner runs flow grant <scope> --autonomy high in a TTY THE SYSTEM SHALL record the grant in ~/.flow/manager/grants.json, and WHEN it runs without a TTY or from an agent session it SHALL refuse
WHEN a pipeline is covered by more than one live grant THE SYSTEM SHALL apply the most specific one (pipeline over epic over repo)
WHEN f1, f5, or the manager writes a decision THE SYSTEM SHALL append it to ~/.flow/manager/log.jsonl with slug, repo, and optional epic, and per-epic readers SHALL see only their epic's entries
WHEN every pipeline a note names is terminal THE SYSTEM SHALL drop the note on the next prune
WHEN a log entry is older than 90 days THE SYSTEM SHALL roll it into per-month counts by kind and outcome, and SHALL never prune an open proposal
WHEN flow epic launch is given --context-file THE SYSTEM SHALL place a delimited Rulings and context block before the seed's pointer sentence

features.title: Wait node: the sequencer has driven one real wave
features.description:
Wait node — do not build anything. This node is satisfied when the epic sequencer from `f1-epic-sequencer` (`flow epic manage`) has driven one real feature from launch to merged on a real epic (this epic's `f2-manager-home` or any econ-data epic feature), with no hand `flow feature create`, launch, or bind for that feature and no drift halt left unexplained in the sequencer's log. It exists so the sequencer is not given the global manager (`f3-global-manager`) until it is proven. The owner records it with `flow epic bind re-design-epic-manager-agent w1-managed-wave --external "<PR of that feature>"`. If a pipeline was launched from this node by mistake, make no code change, stop at triage as no-change, and report that this node must be bound with `flow epic bind ... --external` instead.

Part of epic `re-design-epic-manager-agent` (feature `w1-managed-wave`) — design at `.flow/epics/re-design-epic-manager-agent/design.md`.
features.rationale: Hides D7 (first condition): delegated answers are not built until the sequencer has proven itself on a real wave; enforced by the frontier, not by prose.
acceptanceCriteria: WHEN the owner binds this node with flow epic bind --external THE SYSTEM SHALL classify it merged and unblock f3-global-manager
WHEN this node is unbound THE SYSTEM SHALL never launch it (flow epic launch refuses a waitFor node)
features.waitFor: one feature launched by flow epic manage and merged with no hand launch or bind and no unexplained drift halt

features.title: `flow manage`: one conversational manager over every pipeline, woken only when something changes
features.description:
Build the single global manager the owner talks to. `flow manage [--scope <scope>…] [--model] [--effort] [--heartbeat <dur>] [--stop-when-idle]` opens tmux window `manager` running a Claude session seeded with the new `/flow-manage` skill (the front door; the owner can also say the scope in plain words, saved to f2's `scope.json`). Singleton like f1 (a second start points at `flow attach manager`); model/effort resolve like f5 (flag > `config.models.manager` / `config.efforts.manager` > opus/high). Waking: a zero-token background waiter `flow-manager-wait` (precedent: `flow-plan-review-wait`) discovers pipelines dynamically from every `~/.flow/state/*.json` on each poll (every repo; never a fixed slug list), keeps the last-seen phase per slug, and exits — waking the session — only on a per-slug TRANSITION into a decision point: `plan-pending-review`, `gated`, `needs-human`, any `*-pending-interview` / `*-clarification`, `checkpoint-pending-clear`, `merged`, `cancelled`, a new pipeline, or a pipeline whose state file disappears. A pipeline already sitting at `gated` never re-fires. CI-wait phases never wake it. A heartbeat (`--heartbeat`, `config.manager.heartbeatSec`, default 15 min) makes one batched `gh` query for out-of-band merges and is not a model call. `--stop-when-idle` (off by default, since waiting costs nothing) ends the session when every in-scope pipeline waits on the owner or is done. On each wake the manager reads only: the PR body sections (TLDR, User-facing changes, System changes, Deviations from plan, Test Steps), `plan.md` Open Questions and candidate follow-ups, the pipeline's last pause block slots (Unsolved / Needs attention / Manual action / Untracked), and state phase + age. It reads no diffs, and reads a raw transcript only for a pipeline stuck with no pause block. It may run targeted read-only checks before deciding (download PR screenshots, `git diff <sha> <sha> -- <file>`, one grep). Its job is coordination of big things: carry one pipeline's discovery into another's plan, notice a design gone stale after a sibling merged, shared-resource conflicts (a DB reset vs a seed), manual steps, and stale pipelines (no transition in 7 days ⇒ a cancel proposal, never an automatic cancel). Code-overlap coordination stays the pipelines' job. Messages: non-authority messages (`continue` for `checkpoint-pending-clear`, context, warnings) go as plain peer messages; authority messages (approve, redirect) are a ruling file `~/.flow/manager/rulings/<id>.json` naming the slug, the phase it answers, the reply, and the reason, plus a peer message pointing at it. The pipeline accepts a ruling only after `flow-exec-review ruling --slug <s> --id <id>` confirms a live grant covers it, the ruling names this slug and its current phase, and it is unexpired and not a one-way door; otherwise it ignores it and stays paused. Before every send, the manager checks f2's `scope.json`. Never `send-keys`. The owner's words in the manager window count as owner approval: under a live grant for that scope they become a ruling with `source: owner`; without one the manager names the window to answer in. Interviews and clarifications are never answered alone: the manager drafts a recommended answer into `proposals.json` and the owner accepts with one word. Gated PRs: the manager may tick a `SUBJECTIVE:` item it verified, writing `agent-verified: <evidence>` under it; UI-taste items go through f4. For UI pipelines the manager also records a cross-pipeline consistency note (does this match sibling UI changes and the epic's design direction?) that f4's evidence reads; it does not repeat the pipeline's UI/UX taste review. Epic groups: on every observed merge one f5 wave review (`flow-exec-review review --kind wave`) reorders unstarted features only; anything else is a proposal. Context: every decision is written to f2's log the moment it is made; at the end of each wake the manager runs `/flow-checkpoint` (add a `manager` pane kind to `bin/flow-checkpoint.ts` and the session-start hook), so the owner can `/clear` whenever they like. Owner surface: a status table on each wake that changed something (needs-you items first, oldest first, each with its waiting age), a digest ('N decisions made for you since you last looked'), and a daily `flow-notify` reminder while any needs-you item is older than one day. Spend: f5's $3 cap per call plus a daily cap (`config.manager.dailyBudgetUsd`, default 20) that, when reached, stops executive calls, degrades every decision to the owner, and sends one alert. f1 stays the zero-token board and epic launcher; the manager launches epic features only through f1 or `flow epic launch`. Tests next door: transition-only triggering (already-gated never re-fires), dynamic discovery of a new state file, CI phases ignored, heartbeat makes no model call, scope check refuses an out-of-scope send, ruling verification refuses a stale phase / no grant / wrong slug, checkpoint pane kind, daily cap degrades to the owner, stale-pipeline proposal never cancels.

Part of epic `re-design-epic-manager-agent` (feature `f3-global-manager`) — design at `.flow/epics/re-design-epic-manager-agent/design.md`.
features.rationale: Hides how one long-running conversational manager stays cheap (zero tokens while idle: it wakes only on transitions), safe (scope check, rulings verified by the pipeline, no send-keys), and forgettable (decisions on disk, /flow-checkpoint each wake, the owner clears at will). Owner 2026-11-03: one global manager, selectively scoped; loose pipelines with no epic are fully in scope.
acceptanceCriteria: WHEN a pipeline transitions into a decision phase THE SYSTEM SHALL wake the manager once, and WHEN a pipeline is already in that phase on the next poll it SHALL not wake it again
WHEN a new pipeline state file appears in any repo THE SYSTEM SHALL include it on the next poll without a restart
WHEN a pipeline is in a CI-wait phase THE SYSTEM SHALL not wake the manager, and the heartbeat SHALL make no model call
WHEN the manager is about to message a pipeline outside its saved scope THE SYSTEM SHALL refuse the send
WHEN a pipeline receives a ruling with no live grant covering it, for a different slug, or for a phase it is no longer in THE SYSTEM SHALL ignore it and stay paused
WHEN the manager makes a decision THE SYSTEM SHALL write it to the decision log before the wake ends, and SHALL run /flow-checkpoint at the end of the wake
WHEN an interview or clarification is pending THE SYSTEM SHALL draft a recommended answer as a proposal and never answer it without the owner
WHEN the daily spend cap is reached THE SYSTEM SHALL stop executive calls, send one alert, and leave every decision to the owner
WHEN a needs-you item is older than one day THE SYSTEM SHALL show its waiting age and send one daily reminder

features.title: Wait node: the `## UI review` section has shipped
features.description:
Wait node — do not build anything. This node is satisfied when the PR from the separate flow pipeline `add-ui-ux-critique-improve` has merged; that pipeline adds the machine-written `## UI review` section (a critic's remaining findings, every `SUBJECTIVE:` line left unticked) that `f4-delegated-ui-signoff` reads as evidence. On 2026-10-25 it was at `plan-pending-review` with no PR. The owner records it with `flow epic bind re-design-epic-manager-agent w2-ui-review-section --external "<that PR>"`. If a pipeline was launched from this node by mistake, make no code change, stop at triage as no-change, and report that this node must be bound with `flow epic bind ... --external` instead.

Part of epic `re-design-epic-manager-agent` (feature `w2-ui-review-section`) — design at `.flow/epics/re-design-epic-manager-agent/design.md`.
features.rationale: Hides D7 (second condition): delegated UI sign-off reads a section another pipeline is still building; the frontier waits for it.
acceptanceCriteria: WHEN the owner binds this node with flow epic bind --external THE SYSTEM SHALL classify it merged and unblock f4-delegated-ui-signoff
WHEN this node is unbound THE SYSTEM SHALL never launch it (flow epic launch refuses a waitFor node)
features.waitFor: the PR from pipeline add-ui-ux-critique-improve merged (adds the ## UI review section)

features.title: Evidence-first `SUBJECTIVE:` sign-off: one-action by default, delegated on a second opt-in
features.description:
Make `SUBJECTIVE:` UI sign-off evidence-first, and let a managed epic's pipeline tick those items itself only under a second explicit owner opt-in with a non-Claude reviewer agreeing. Default (no extra grant, every pipeline): when step 9's `flow-gate-decide` returns `gated` with `SUBJECTIVE:` items open, the GATED block (`flow-gate-summary`) carries, per item, the screenshots for every viewport and theme it names and the `## UI review` summary, so the owner judges and ticks in one action without hunting. Delegated (class `subjective`, granted only by `flow grant <scope> --autonomy high --delegate-ui` (f2's scoped grant store; `flow epic grant <epic> … --delegate-ui` is its alias)): before rendering GATED, an epic feature runs `flow-exec-review review --kind ui` (f5's executive review with the charter's end-user-expectation lens), which approves only when the PR body's `## UI review` section exists with no remaining `major` or `defect` finding, screenshots exist for every viewport and theme each open item names, a non-Claude reviewer — Gemini 4 Argon (High) via `flow-delegate` — independently views the screenshots and agrees with the in-pipeline UI critique (fail closed when `flow-delegate` is unavailable or cannot read the images: reuse `bin/lib/agy-cooldown.ts` and `bin/lib/delegate-skip-class.ts`, leave the item for the owner, retry once the cooldown ends, and report the outage in the manager digest — never fall back to a Claude-only tick), the manager's cross-pipeline consistency note (from `f3-global-manager`, when present) raises no conflict, and no `DECISION:` or `Browser:` item and no other gate reason is open. There is no second same-model taste review: the pipeline's own UI/UX review is the Claude view, Argon is the second. Pass ⇒ tick only those `SUBJECTIVE:` items, post one evidence comment on the PR (screenshots, critique summary, reviewer verdict, decision id), record the decision in the epic log, then take a NEW non-override branch in `skills/pipeline/flow-pipeline/references/phases/step-09-gate.md`: re-run `flow-gate-decide "$PR"`; `auto-merge` (all items ticked, `autoMerge` not false) ⇒ step 10, with the log entry stating the merge came from a gate re-check under `autoMerge`, not from any instruction; anything else ⇒ route per the normal table. It never calls `flow-merge-guard --record-override`, never fires the gate-override form, and with `autoMerge: false` still stops at `gated` for the owner's 'merge'. Fail ⇒ the default evidence block plus one line naming the failed precondition. Narrow AGENTS.md's 'SUBJECTIVE: approval step the agent can't tick' rule, `references/output-style.md`, and `skills/pipeline/flow-pr-review/references/manual-test-rubric.md` to name this single exception (owner grant + second opt-in + non-Claude agreement), and anchor it in `bin/skill-md-lint.test.ts`. Tests next door: evidence-block rendering, each precondition's fail path, reviewer-unavailable fail-closed, `DECISION:`/`Browser:` never ticked, the re-check branch reaching step 10 only on `auto-merge`, and `autoMerge: false` staying gated.

Part of epic `re-design-epic-manager-agent` (feature `f4-delegated-ui-signoff`) — design at `.flow/epics/re-design-epic-manager-agent/design.md`.
features.rationale: Hides D6: the UI evidence bar, the non-Claude agreement check, and the non-override gate re-check that is the only path from a delegated tick to a merge.
acceptanceCriteria: WHEN a PR is gated with SUBJECTIVE items open and no subjective grant THE SYSTEM SHALL render the screenshots per named viewport and theme and the UI review summary in the GATED block

WHEN the subjective class is granted and the evidence bar holds and the non-Claude reviewer agrees THE SYSTEM SHALL tick only the SUBJECTIVE items, post one evidence comment, record the decision, and re-run flow-gate-decide
WHEN the re-check returns auto-merge THE SYSTEM SHALL proceed to step 10 and log that the merge came from a gate re-check under autoMerge, and WHEN autoMerge is false it SHALL stay gated
WHEN a DECISION or Browser item is open, the UI review has a major or defect finding, a named screenshot is missing, or flow-delegate cannot read the images THE SYSTEM SHALL not tick anything
THE SYSTEM SHALL never call flow-merge-guard --record-override or fire the gate-override form on this path (lint anchor in bin/skill-md-lint.test.ts)

WHEN a Claude-side model call is made for a delegated UI sign-off THE SYSTEM SHALL use the model and effort resolved like the manager's model: the sequencer's `--model`/`--effort` when it passes them, else `config.models.manager` / `config.efforts.manager`, else opus/high

features.title: Follow-ups land in exactly one place: an epic proposal, a GitHub issue the manager files, or a logged drop
features.description:
Let the global manager (from `f3-global-manager`) own follow-ups so nothing discovered mid-run is lost. Sources: the pause block's Untracked slot, `plan.md` candidate follow-ups (including unticked ones, which today die with the worktree — `skills/pipeline/flow-pipeline/references/phases/step-10-merge.md` files only ticked ones), PR `## Deviations from plan` and Test Steps manual items, and things the owner discusses in the manager window. Routing, one place per item: (a) it fits a live epic's goal ⇒ a PROPOSED epic addition in f2's `proposals.json`; (b) worth doing but no epic fits ⇒ a GitHub issue the manager files on its own in the owner's repos, preflighted with `flow-create-issue` (value rubric), deduplicated against open issues and live manifests, labelled `flow-manager`, and linked to its source PR; (c) below the bar ⇒ dropped, with a one-line reason in the decision log and the digest so the owner can overrule. Managing issues: dedupe, link, close an issue when a merged PR fixes it (with a comment naming the PR), and move an issue into an epic once the owner accepts the epic proposal (close it with a link). Epic updates — add, cut, defer a feature, or change the goal — are always proposals the owner approves; unstarted-feature reordering stays autonomous (f5 wave review). On an owner yes the manager writes the amendment in a separate worktree (never the canonical checkout), validates it with `flow-epic-manifest-schema --validate` and `flow-epic-dag --validate`, and opens a manifest-only PR; with a live merge grant for that repo (`f7-merge-grant`) it may merge that PR, otherwise the owner merges. Tests next door: each routing branch, unticked candidates captured before the worktree is removed, dedupe against an open issue and a manifest feature, close-on-merge comment, an epic change never applied without an owner yes, amendment written outside the canonical checkout.

Part of epic `re-design-epic-manager-agent` (feature `f6-followup-routing`) — design at `.flow/epics/re-design-epic-manager-agent/design.md`.
features.rationale: Hides the routing rule between epic proposals, issues, and drops. Owner 2026-11-05: the manager may create and manage GitHub issues on their behalf with its own judgment of the bar, but epic updates are proposed and approved by the owner.
acceptanceCriteria: WHEN a follow-up fits a live epic's goal THE SYSTEM SHALL record an epic-addition proposal and SHALL not edit the manifest until the owner says yes

WHEN a follow-up fits no epic and meets the bar THE SYSTEM SHALL file one GitHub issue through flow-create-issue, labelled flow-manager and linked to its source PR, unless an open issue or manifest feature already covers it
WHEN a follow-up is below the bar THE SYSTEM SHALL log a one-line drop reason and show it in the digest
WHEN a merged PR fixes an open flow-manager issue THE SYSTEM SHALL close it with a comment naming the PR
WHEN the owner approves an epic change THE SYSTEM SHALL write and validate the amendment in a separate worktree and open a manifest-only PR

features.title: A merge grant: the manager can merge a verified PR in place of the owner's override, never a one-way door
features.description:
Let the owner open merging to the manager, per repo. `flow grant repo:<name> --merge` (TTY-only, f2's grant store). With a live merge grant, `bin/flow-merge-guard.ts` accepts a manager merge ruling (from `f3-global-manager`) in place of the owner's gate-override token when ALL hold: every Test Step is ticked, each manager tick carries `agent-verified: <evidence>`; no `DECISION:` item is open; CI is green on the head SHA; review has finished; a non-Claude reviewer (Gemini 4 Argon (High) via `flow-delegate`, reusing f4's evidence check) agreed with the evidence; and the PR is not a one-way door. One-way doors are DB migrations, infrastructure applies (terraform), secrets / IAM, billing, usage counters, and shared or production data. They are detected without any notes file: (a) parse the repo's `.github/workflows/*.yml` for push-to-default-branch triggers whose jobs apply migrations or infrastructure, and match the PR's files against their `paths`; (b) built-in patterns (`**/migrations/**`, `*.tf`, `infrastructure/terraform/**`); (c) the PR's `## System changes` naming any one-way class. An unparseable workflow fails closed. Ordinary app code that deploys through CD stays mergeable: auto-merge already ships it without the owner today, and rollback is a revert. Evidence (econ-data, last 40 merged PRs, sampled 2026-11-07): 20 touched `backend/`, 21 the frontend (`src/`, `static/`), 5 `supabase/migrations/`, 11 `infrastructure/terraform|monitoring/` — a deploy-path rule would block almost every econ-data PR; the one-way rule blocks the 16 that matter. The merge itself still runs in the pipeline's own step 10 (merge-resolver, post-merge sweep), and posts the same disclosure comment as today's override path plus the ruling id. A manifest-only PR (f6 amendments) touches no deploy path and is mergeable under the grant. Under a live merge grant, the manager may also launch new pipelines with auto-merge on. Rewrite the hard rules 'never merge on the manager's own instruction' (charter text seeded by f5, AGENTS.md) and `/flow-epic-run`'s 'Never merge a feature PR' to 'never merge without the owner's merge grant'; `flow-merge-guard --record-override` stays owner-only. AGENTS.md is at its size budget: replace text, do not add. Argon outages: reuse `bin/lib/agy-cooldown.ts` and `bin/lib/delegate-skip-class.ts`; Argon unavailable ⇒ the merge stays the owner's, retried once the cooldown ends, reported in the digest. Tests next door: each precondition's fail path, migration / terraform / System-changes one-way detection, unparseable workflow fails closed, app-code PR mergeable, manifest-only PR mergeable, disclosure comment with ruling id, Argon unavailable ⇒ owner, no grant ⇒ today's behaviour.

Part of epic `re-design-epic-manager-agent` (feature `f7-merge-grant`) — design at `.flow/epics/re-design-epic-manager-agent/design.md`.
features.rationale: Hides the merge-grant check and the one-way-door detector. Owner 2026-11-05: wants the manager able to merge where appropriate; merge scope 'go with your best judgement' ⇒ flow fully, econ-data minus one-way doors. Last in the DAG because it is the highest-blast-radius autonomy.
acceptanceCriteria: WHEN a live merge grant covers the repo and every precondition holds THE SYSTEM SHALL let flow-merge-guard accept the manager's ruling in place of an override token and post the disclosure comment with the ruling id
WHEN a PR changes a migration, an infrastructure apply path, or names a one-way class in System changes THE SYSTEM SHALL refuse the manager ruling and leave the merge to the owner
WHEN a workflow file cannot be parsed THE SYSTEM SHALL treat the PR as a one-way door
WHEN a DECISION item is open, CI is not green, review is unfinished, or the non-Claude reviewer did not agree THE SYSTEM SHALL refuse the manager ruling
WHEN the non-Claude reviewer is unavailable (quota, outage, timeout, refusal) THE SYSTEM SHALL leave the merge to the owner, retry after the agy cooldown ends, and report it in the digest
THE SYSTEM SHALL never let an agent call flow-merge-guard --record-override
